validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed, not a phantom. Three mutually-independent primary documents agree on the same project: (1) PNGRB's own Annual Report 2019-20, p.46, section 3.8 'Cancellation of authorisations' (https://www.pngrb.gov.in/pdf/annualreports/eng2019-2020.pdf) states 'Ennore-Nellore Natural Gas Pipeline: Authorization issued on 2nd December, 2014 ... in favour of Gas Transmission India Private Limited (GTIL) had to be cancelled by the Board on 30th October, 2019 ... Subsequently, the order ... has been challenged by GTIL before the APTEL' (a PBG of Rs.7.3 crore/730 lakh was encashed, reconciling internally with the report's own PBG-litigation table on p.90). (2) PNGRB's live NGPL MIS Report, 31 May 2026 edition (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, row 1 of the under-construction section: 'Ennore-Nellore  GTIL  02.12.2014  220  36.0 ... 0  220 ... Apr-20  AP & TN') still lists it, matching the sheet's length/capacity exactly. (3) An unrelated APTEL Tribunal judgment dated 26 April 2024 (Appeal Nos. 331/332/361 of 2022 & 13/636/640 of 2023, AGP CGD India Pvt Ltd vs PNGRB — the SAME PDF already cited on the sheet as current_ref for Status/Fuel/PipelineType, https://www.aptel.gov.in/sites/default/files/Jud2024/APL_No_331of2022_&_IA_no_1259_of_2022_APL_No_332_of_2022_&_IA_No_1260_2022_Apl_No_361of2022_&_IA_No_1277_Of_2022.pdf) references 'Ennore-Nellore pipeline (ENPL) which was authorized in December, 2014 and was to be commissioned in April, 2020 ... the authorization of ENPL pipeline was cancelled by PNGRB vide order dated 20th December, 2022 which was upheld by this Tribunal vide its judgement dated 4th October, 2023' as undisputed background fact in an unrelated CGD-bidding dispute. All three agree on authorizing entity (GTIL), authorization date (2 Dec 2014), target (Apr 2020), and route (Ennore, Tamil Nadu -> Nellore, Andhra Pradesh). Note: automated url_verifier FAILs on both PNGRB PDFs and the aptel.gov.in PDF are false negatives of documented patterns (SSL cert-chain error on aptel.gov.in; large-PDF / hyphenation-split-token extraction miss on the two PNGRB PDFs) -- all three manually confirmed live (curl 200) and content-matched via pdftotext -layout / pypdf. CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission common-carrier pipeline -- matches PNGRB's own regulatory classification in every document above. DUPLICATE: checked against all 26 other India-gas roster rows. P0922 (Ennore-Tuticorin-Bengaluru) and P6646 (Ennore-Barshi) share the Ennore origin point but serve entirely different corridors/GAs (Tuticorin/Bengaluru vs Barshi/Maharashtra); PNGRB's own register carries Ennore-Nellore as its own separately-authorized, separately-numbered line (S.No.1 of the under-construction section) distinct from Ennore-Tuticorin (a separate IOCL authorization, 09.12.2018) and from Kakinada-Vijayawada-Nellore (IMC Limited, a different entity/route that happens to also end near Nellore -- matches roster row P1434, not this one). No relabel/double-count found. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 = 'Gas Transmission India Private Ltd' 100% is correct -- confirmed by both PNGRB documents (entity=GTIL) and independently named in the APTEL judgment. SPEC: Capacity 36.00 MMSCMD and LengthKnown 220.00 km match the PNGRB register exactly (delta=0), but PNGRB is the origin of that figure (per country guidance, not an independent second source for the value itself) -- treat as medium-tier corroboration, not a GEM error. CAVEAT (the material finding, detailed fully in status_reviews): GEM's Status='shelved' undersells the record. This is not simply a live-but-dormant authorization sitting on a lapsed 2020 target (the Trap #4 pattern the country note warns about) -- PNGRB's Board formally CANCELLED GTIL's authorization on 30 October 2019 for failure to reach financial closure/gas tie-up (encashing the performance bank guarantee), GTIL's appeal produced a further Board order dated 20 December 2022, and APTEL upheld the cancellation on 4 October 2023 and again treated it as settled in the April 2024 judgment. The PNGRB MIS register simply has not been administratively updated to drop the cancelled line (it still carries the original 2014/2020 authorization dates), which is why it still appears there in 2026.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is an affirmative regulatory-cancellation finding, not a dormancy inference, so the 2y/4y staleness rules do not apply. PNGRB's own Annual Report 2019-20 (p.46, section 3.8 'Cancellation of authorisations') states in its own words: 'Ennore-Nellore Natural Gas Pipeline: Authorization issued on 2nd December, 2014 ... in favour of Gas Transmission India Private Limited (GTIL) had to be cancelled by the Board on 30th October, 2019, under the provision of the extant regulations, as GTIL failed to achieve FC and Capacity booking/Natural Gas Tie-up and there has been virtually no progress in the execution of the pipeline project ... The Performance Bank Guarantee of Rs.7.3 Crore was accordingly encashed by the Board. Subsequently, the order of the Board for cancellation of the authorisation has been challenged by GTIL before the APTEL.' Consistent with this, the same report's own 30-June-2020 'Natural Gas Pipelines under construction' table (Annexure listing) does NOT include Ennore-Nellore at all -- it had already dropped off PNGRB's own live-authorization list within a year of cancellation. The later APTEL judgment (26 April 2024, Appeal Nos. 331/332/361 of 2022 & 13/636/640 of 2023, an unrelated CGD-bidding case that references ENPL only as background) states as settled fact: 'the authorization of ENPL pipeline was cancelled by PNGRB vide order dated 20th December, 2022 which was upheld by this Tribunal vide its judgement dated 4th October, 2023' -- and repeats this a second time later in the same judgment ('ENPL ... cancelled by the Respondent-Board on 20th December, 2022'). Reading the two PNGRB-family documents together, the most coherent procedural picture is: Board cancels (30 Oct 2019) -> GTIL appeals to APTEL -> a further/confirming Board order issues (20 Dec 2022), possibly after remand or renewed default -> APTEL upholds cancellation (4 Oct 2023) -> referenced again as settled in the April 2024 judgment. I could not independently pin down whether the Dec-2022 date is a second cancellation order or the AR2019-20's report of the *original* 30-Oct-2019 date is simply superseded terminology in the later document -- flagging this dating nuance for Update to resolve if precision matters, but it does not affect the bottom-line verdict: BOTH the regulator and its own appellate tribunal treat this authorization as formally and finally dead, well past mere shelving. I set CancelledYear=2019 (the initiating Board order) rather than 2023 (final appellate confirmation) since 2019 is when the Board's cancellation action actually occurred; recommend Update confirm which year GEM's convention prefers (initiating order vs. final-on-appeal) before applying. PNGRB's live May-2026 MIS register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf) still lists the line under 'under construction' with the original 2014/Apr-2020 dates -- this is administrative non-removal of a cancelled authorization (the register apparently isn't purged of formally-cancelled lines, distinct from Trap #4's 'never retires an unsurrendered authorisation' pattern, since here PNGRB itself already acted to cancel it) and should NOT be read as evidence the project is alive. Both PDF url_verifier checks FAIL via the automated script (SSL cert-chain error on aptel.gov.in; large-PDF extraction miss on the multi-hundred-page AR2019-20) but both are documented false-negative patterns in url_verifier.py's own docstring; manually confirmed live (curl 200) and content-matched (pdftotext -layout / pypdf extraction quoted verbatim above).

summary: P0921 Ennore-Nellore Gas Pipeline is real, correctly classified, correctly attributed to sole owner GTIL, not a duplicate of any other roster row, and its 220 km/36 MMSCMD spec matches PNGRB's own register -- but the sheet's own current_ref (an APTEL judgment) actually documents that PNGRB formally CANCELLED GTIL's authorization (Board order 30 Oct 2019, contested, upheld by APTEL 4 Oct 2023, corroborated independently by PNGRB's own Annual Report 2019-20 p.46), so Status should move from shelved to cancelled (ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed) rather than being treated as a live-but-dormant authorization.
